title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (pages 90-92): E and E' are sets, each carrying a family of 'supports'. Σ_E ⊂ P(E) is closed under arbitrary intersections, so it is a closure (Moore) system. Sup°_E(A) is the closure of A, the smallest support containing A. Σ_E ordered by inclusion is a complete lattice, with Sup^{Σ_E} S_i = Sup°_E(∪S_i).

The symbol x |∘| S denotes an incidence or 'apartness' relation between points and supports. Page 92 writes β(x') = ∁γ(x'), which suggests |∘| is a non-membership/disjointness-type relation.

A correspondence α : E → P(E') (a relation) yields:
- α'(x) = Sup°_{E'}(α(x)), the closure of α(x);
- α_*(S) = Sup°_{E'}(ᾱ(S)) = Sup^{Σ_{E'}}_{x∈S} α'(x), where ᾱ(S) = ∪_{x∈S} α(x).
By construction α_* : Σ_E → Σ_{E'} is monotone.

The Proposition states that the following are equivalent:
- (i) α admits a 'transpose' β : E' → P(E). This is equivalently given by β' : E' → Σ_E or β_* : Σ_{E'} → Σ_E. The defining relation, written on p.92, is x |∘| β(x') ⇔ α(x) |∘| x'. Page 90 already shows that the transpose is unique when it exists.
- (ii) α_* preserves arbitrary sups of the lattice Σ_E. Equivalently, for every A ⊂ E, α_*(Sup°_E A) = Sup°_{E'}(ᾱ(A)): the closure of A and A itself have the same closed image. This is the classical continuity condition f(cl A) ⊂ cl f(A), here for multivalued maps. Item (ii)b is the special case for closures of points.
- (iii) For every S' ∈ Σ_{E'}, the set {x ∈ E : α(x) ⊂ S'} lies in Σ_E. This is the 'preimage of a closed set is closed' (upper-inverse) form of continuity.
- (iv) For every x' ∈ E', the set {x : α(x) |∘| x'} lies in Σ_E, i.e. the pointwise version of (iii).

In lattice terms this is the standard fact that a monotone map between complete lattices preserves all sups iff it has a right adjoint. The right adjoint is S' ↦ {x : α(x) ⊂ S'}, and its existence is a Galois connection. The 'transpose' is the Chu-space / polarity-style adjoint relative to the incidence relation |∘|.

The purpose is to determine which correspondences between such 'support spaces' admit a transpose, i.e. to define good morphisms of this structure (a duality or 'transposition' for relations between closure spaces). This presumably feeds the combinatorial/topological constructions of Chapter IX.
errors: Item (ii)b is inserted as an extra condition, but it is just a special case of the formula in the second (ii) (take A = {x}). The numbering of (ii) is duplicated and messy.

Neither this page nor the next spells out precisely what |∘| means between a set and a point, so (iv) ⇔ (iii) depends on the convention, apparently S' = complement-type support of {x'}. Page 92 says '(iii) ⇒ (iv) trivial, taking S' = cosupp{x'}', which presupposes that such a support exists and is characterized by |∘|. This is not stated on this page.

ideas.what: Equivalence for a relation between closure spaces: induced map on closed-set lattices preserves arbitrary sups ⇔ inverse images of closed sets are closed ⇔ existence of an adjoint 'transposed' relation
ideas.modern_name: Galois connection / adjoint functor theorem for complete lattices (sup-lattice morphisms); continuity of multivalued maps between closure spaces (upper semicontinuity)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ore (1944) and Birkhoff for Galois connections; Moore/Birkhoff for closure systems; Joyal-Tierney for sup-lattices; Kuratowski/Berge for semicontinuity of multifunctions

ideas.what: Transposition of correspondences relative to an incidence relation x |∘| S (x |∘| β(x') ⇔ α(x) |∘| x')
ideas.modern_name: Chu-space morphism / adjoint pair with respect to a polarity (formal concept analysis)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Barr and Chu (1979); Wille and Ganter (formal concept analysis, 1980s)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but standard order-theoretic lemma: sup-preserving maps between complete lattices of closed sets correspond to adjoints and transposed relations. It is classical in lattice theory and closure-space continuity. Its only interest is as a building block of Grothendieck's 1986 'Ateliers' notes, not as new mathematics.

The second (ii) reads 'Ou la formule, pour A ∈ P(E): α_*(Sup°_E(A)) = Sup°_{E'}(ᾱ(A)) (i.e. ᾱ(Ā) et ᾱ(A) ont même support dans E')'. The overbrace labels Sup°_E(A) as Ā; 'sup-parfait[?]' should read 'même support'.
